# Oliveira–Pich–Santhanam: under NP ⊆ P/poly, anti-checkers are generated by near-linear circuits

Assume $\mathrm{NP} \subseteq \mathrm{P/poly}$. Then there is a constant $k$ such that for every sufficiently small $\beta > 0$ and all large $n$ there is a circuit of size at most $2^{n + k\beta n}$ that maps the truth table of any $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ to a list of $\lfloor 2^{10\beta n} \rfloor$ inputs such that, if $\mathrm{CC}(f) > \lfloor 2^{\beta n} \rfloor$, then every circuit of size at most $\lfloor 2^{\beta n}/(10n) \rfloor$ errs on one of the listed inputs (Oliveira, Pich and Santhanam 2019, Lemma 17, the Anti-Checker Lemma).

## Proof sketch

Build the anti-checker greedily: maintain a set of candidate small circuits consistent with $f$ on the inputs chosen so far, and repeatedly add an input that eliminates at least a $1/(2n)$ fraction of them while many remain; the few survivors are then listed and refuted directly. Deciding thresholds on the number of consistent circuits is an NP-type (approximate counting / hashing) question, so under $\mathrm{NP} \subseteq \mathrm{P/poly}$ the oracle queries of this greedy procedure are answered by polynomial-size circuits, giving the stated total size.
